The prompt the chain was sent:

Only long-running or background commands should show in the @{SubagentsPanel} (and obviously subagents)  The intent is to display like, non-foreground kinds of things, so we still get feedback even if the main thread is paused or finished while other things are going on.

What the spec step said it changed, its final output:

I changed the spec so the SubagentsPanel shows only work going on apart from the main thread, plus ordinary commands once they've run long. `piton check` reports no problems, `piton build` wrote 79 files, and the new text appears in the refreshed reference.

**"Long-running" means 15 seconds.** That was my choice; it's one number in the spec if you want it shorter or longer.

## What changed in the spec

All edits are in `spec/ui/components/right-sidebar/subagents/index.pi`, the `description` section (`.claude/reference/ui/components/right-sidebar/subagents/index.md#description`).

- **Purpose:** the panel is for what goes on apart from the main thread, so you still see it while the main thread waits, pauses or has finished its turn.
- **Subagents:** every subagent is shown, whether the main thread waits on it or it runs in the background.
- **Commands:**
  - Background commands are always shown.
  - An ordinary command (a Bash call the main thread waits on) appears only once it has run 15 seconds without its result coming back. Its time counts from when it started, and it sits among the other rows by start time.
  - A command that finishes within 15 seconds never appears, not even briefly.
- **Never shown:** commands a subagent runs, and every other tool call. All of them stay in the task's output table as before; the panel just leaves them out.
- **Long waited-on commands:**
  - They don't hold the run open.
  - They end when their result comes back, done or failed, or when the run ends.
  - Their tooltip kind reads "Command, waited on".
  - They have no Stop button, since only background tasks can be stopped on their own. The task's Cancel button still stops them.
- **Subagents the main thread waits on:**
  - They end when the harness reports their end, or when their tool call's result comes back, whichever is first.
  - They can be stopped only where the harness gave them a task id. Otherwise they have no Stop button.
- **Showing the panel:** it appears once the run has something to show in it, not before.

The constraints are in `.suspense/history/1791131709-FilterSubagentsPanelForBackground.understanding.md`.

## Anchors the code should follow
- `SubagentsPanel`: `#description` for the filtering and the 15-second rule. `#elapsed`, `#stopping` and `#by-mode` are unchanged but apply to the new rows.
- `HarnessIntegrationScope`: `#feeding`, for how background tasks are tracked and stopped by id.
- `TaskTableScope`: `#types`. All tool calls, short commands included, stay in the task's output table.

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors still need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings before they can be used. None of them were needed here.

content.content:
#### Description

It lists the background tasks the harness started for the run, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../../../scope/harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) keeps them: its subagents, the agents it started, and its background commands, the shell commands it ran in the background, such as a long build. A background task of any other kind isn't shown.
It is for what goes on apart from the run's main thread, so that while the main thread is waiting, paused, or has finished its turn, what is still going on is still seen. Every subagent is shown, whether the harness waits on it or runs it in the background. A command is shown only when it runs in the background, or when it runs long, as follows. An ordinary command the main thread waits on, a Bash tool call not run in the background, is never shown while it is short, and is shown only once it has been running for 15 seconds without its result coming back, from then until it ends, its time counting from its start as any row's does, its row taking its place among the others by when it started. A short command, done within those 15 seconds, never appears at all, not even for a moment, and neither does a command a subagent runs, which is part of that subagent's work, nor any other tool call. All of them are still rows of the task's output, as the [TaskTableScope](../../task-table/index.md#task-table-scope) says; this panel only leaves them out.
A long command the main thread waits on isn't a background task: it doesn't hold the run open, and it ends when its tool call's result comes back, done or failed as that result says, or when the run ends, as the run did. Its tooltip's kind reads "Command, waited on". It has no Stop button, since the harness can stop only a background task on its own; the task's Cancel button stops it with the run.
A subagent the main thread waits on ends when the harness notifies its end, or else when its tool call's result comes back, whichever comes first, and can be stopped as a background one can wherever the harness gave it a task id, its Stop button left out otherwise.
It is shown only once the run has something to show in it, and takes no room before. One row per subagent or command shown, in the order they started, subagents and commands together, each 24 pixels tall, 8 pixels in from the panel's edges: a spinner while it is at work, then a tick, a cross, or a dash for how it ended, done, failed, or stopped, beside a small icon for its kind, a robot for a subagent and a terminal for a command, in the theme's muted grey, then what it was started to do, in small text, cut off with an ellipsis, muted once it has ended. For a subagent that is its description, and for a command the command itself, on one line, in monospace. Its tooltip gives what it was started to do, and beneath, muted, its kind, "Subagent" or "Command", and what it is doing or how it ended. The panel is only as tall as its rows need, up to 30% of the sidebar's height, scrolling beyond that.

#### Elapsed
#### Stopping

A row at work can be stopped, from a Stop button: a small ghost button with a stop icon, 18 pixels square, which takes the place of its running time while the row is hovered, whose tooltip reads "Stop this subagent" or "Stop this command". Clicking it stops only that background task, as the [HarnessIntegrationScope](../../../../scope/harness-integration/index.md#harness-integration-scope) says: the task the run is for and every other background task carry on, and nothing else in the panel or the task's output changes. Once clicked, the button is disabled and the row's spinner stays until the harness notifies its end, when it shows a dash for stopped, as any stopped one does. A row that has ended has no Stop button, and neither does one whose run can't stop it on its own, as one whose input is already closed, where the task's own Cancel button stops everything still going.

#### By Mode

content.text:
All 511 tests pass. The panel now leaves out what the main thread is busy with and shows what goes on apart from it. I haven't run a real task to watch a 15-second command appear.

- **Subagents:** every subagent shows, whether it runs in the background or the main thread waits on it.
- **Background commands:** always show, from when the harness reports them, with the command itself as the text.
- **Commands the main thread waits on:**
  - **When it shows:** a regular Bash call shows only once it has run 15 seconds with no result. One that finishes sooner never appears.
  - **Once shown:** it stays listed after it ends, showing how long it ran. It ends done or failed when its result comes back, or when the run ends.
  - **Tooltip and Stop:** its tooltip reads "Command, waited on", and it has no Stop button.
- **Never shown:** commands a subagent runs, and all other tool calls. They still appear in the task's output as before.
- **Subagents the main thread waits on:** they end when the harness reports their end or their result comes back, whichever comes first. They get a Stop button only once the harness has given them a task id.
- **When the panel appears:** the sidebar now waits until there's a row to show. A run full of short commands doesn't bring it out.

What I had to work out:
- **Matching a waited-on subagent to its task:** when the harness reports a waited-on subagent as a task too, I match it to the existing row by its tool call id, so it doesn't appear twice. If the harness gives no tool call id, I match by description instead.
- **What counts as a command or a subagent:** a "Bash" tool call is a command, and an "Agent" or "Task" call is a subagent. Calls with `run_in_background` set are left to the harness's own report of the background task, since their result comes back straight away.

Most of the change is in `src/subagents.rs`, with the panel filtering in `src/referenced_spec.rs` and the sidebar check in `src/prompt_mode.rs`. I added tests for each of these rules. The spec and the prompt agree, including the spec step's choice of 15 seconds for "long-running".

The Gmail, Google Calendar and Google Drive connectors still need authorizing in your claude.ai connector settings, and the `backlog` MCP server didn't start. None of them were needed here.
